outline.chapter_title: Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models: Context and Goals
outline.description: Introduce why RL is used to scale LLM capabilities, the stability challenges at large scale, and the paper’s central contribution: GSPO as a stable, efficient alternative to token-weighted objectives.
subtopics: Why RL for LLMs: deep reasoning, math, coding, multi-step synthesis
Stability as the bottleneck when scaling compute, length, and model size
Observed collapse in state-of-the-art methods (e.g., GRPO) on large models
High-level preview of GSPO: sequence-level importance ratios and clipping
Roadmap of the textbook

outline.chapter_title: Preliminaries: Notation, Setup, and Baseline Algorithms
outline.description: Establish the formal RL-for-LLM setup, key notation, and summarize PPO and GRPO as widely used baselines.
subtopics: Autoregressive policy πθ, queries x, responses y, sequence likelihood πθ(y|x)
Reward model/verifier r(x,y) in [0,1]
Off-policy updates with rollout batches and mini-batching
PPO objective: token-level importance ratio, clipping, and value model dependency
Challenges of PPO for LLMs: compute, memory, value accuracy
GRPO objective: group-based advantages without a value model
Group size G, per-response z-score advantage, token-level weighting in GRPO

outline.chapter_title: Diagnosing Instability: Why Token-Level Importance Weighting Breaks
outline.description: Explain the paper’s core diagnosis: GRPO’s token-level importance weighting misapplies importance sampling, causing high-variance gradients and collapse.
subtopics: Importance sampling principle: estimating expectations under target vs behavior distributions
Need for averaging over many samples per distribution to reduce variance
Token-level weighting in GRPO: single-sample next-token correction is ineffective
Variance accumulation over long sequences and amplification by clipping
Empirical symptom: irreversible model collapse despite hyperparameter rescue attempts
Key design principle: align unit of optimization with unit of reward (sequence)

outline.description: Present the GSPO objective, its sequence-level importance ratio, and how clipping and advantage normalization are applied at the sequence level.
subtopics: Sequence-level objective with response-wise clipping
Group-based normalized advantages (z-score within a query’s responses)
Sequence-level importance ratio si(θ) = [πθ(y|x)/πold(y|x)]^(1/|y|)
Length normalization: controlling variance and unified clipping scales
How GSPO matches reward granularity and off-policy correction
Choosing clipping ranges: different magnitude vs token-level methods
Intuition: fewer, more meaningful weights; exclude overly off-policy responses

outline.description: Derive and interpret the gradients, highlighting how GSPO equalizes token weights within a response versus GRPO’s per-token reweighting.
subtopics: Unclipped gradient of GSPO: response-level weight times average token log-gradients
Unclipped gradient of GRPO: per-token importance-weighted gradients
Consequence: GSPO equal token weights per response; GRPO unequal token weights
Why unequal token weights accumulate instability over time in GRPO
Effect on variance and sample efficiency

outline.description: Introduce GSPO-token for finer-grained advantage shaping, while retaining GSPO’s stable sequence-level weighting through stop-gradient constructs.
subtopics: Objective with per-token advantages and sequence-informed token weights
Stop-gradient trick: numerical equality to si(θ) with stable gradients
Equivalence to GSPO when token advantages are uniform
Use cases: multi-turn RL, localized credit assignment
Trade-offs and when to prefer GSPO vs GSPO-token

outline.description: Provide actionable guidance on applying GSPO in LLM RL: batching, off-policy effects, hyperparameters, and stability heuristics.
subtopics: Rollout generation under πold and mini-batch updates (off-policy reality)
Setting clipping ranges for sequence-level ratios
Group size G and reward normalization effects
KL regularization: role and typical settings (even though omitted in derivation)
Length control and generation constraints
Compute/memory considerations: no value model, sequence-likelihood computation
Monitoring: sequence ratio statistics, clipped fraction of responses, rewards

outline.description: Summarize and interpret the reported results on rewards and benchmarks; relate findings to the theoretical claims about variance and efficiency.
subtopics: Benchmarks: AIME’24, LiveCodeBench, CodeForces (Elo)
Training curves: stability over long runs, scaling with more compute and length
Efficiency: higher training accuracy and downstream metrics vs GRPO under equal compute
Cold-start on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base: practical implications
Clipping fraction observation: GSPO clips far more tokens yet learns faster
Interpretation: GRPO’s token-level gradients are noisy; GSPO’s signal is cleaner

outline.description: Explain why MoE exacerbates GRPO instability, the prior workaround (Routing Replay), and how GSPO inherently resolves it.
subtopics: Sparse activation and expert-activation volatility across updates
Effect on token-level ratios: unstable per-token likelihoods with changing experts
Routing Replay: caching old routing to restore comparability in GRPO
Costs of Routing Replay: memory, communication, capacity constraints
GSPO’s robustness: sequence likelihoods remain stable despite token-level routing changes
Empirical outcome: normal convergence without Routing Replay

outline.description: Discuss how sequence-level likelihoods allow avoiding recomputation under training engines, aiding disaggregated training-inference setups.
subtopics: Precision mismatches between training and inference engines
GSPO’s tolerance: using inference-engine sequence log-likelihoods directly
Benefits in partial rollout, multi-turn RL, and disaggregated systems
Operational simplifications and potential throughput gains

outline.description: Provide a step-by-step guide to implement GSPO in practice, including data flow, key computations, and common pitfalls.
subtopics: End-to-end loop: sample with πold → score rewards → compute si(θ), Âi → clip → update θ
Efficient sequence log-prob computation and caching
Numerical stability: log-space sums, length normalization, epsilon handling
Choice of optimizer and schedule; gradient accumulation with large batches
Diagnostics: distribution of si(θ), clipped ratios, reward stats, loss decomposition
Common errors: mixing token- and sequence-level ratios; mis-scaled clipping; missing stop-gradient in GSPO-token

outline.description: Critically assess GSPO’s scope, possible extensions, and research directions prompted by the findings.
subtopics: When GSPO-token’s finer credit assignment helps or hurts
Interaction with KL penalties, baselines, and other regularizers
Reward model drift and non-stationarity
Handling extremely long sequences and memory constraints
Theoretical analysis opportunities: variance bounds, convergence in off-policy regimes
Generalization to non-autoregressive or structured generation tasks

outline.description: Recap the motivation, algorithm, and empirical evidence, emphasizing the design principle of sequence-aligned optimization.
subtopics: Sequence-level importance weighting aligns with sequence rewards
Equalized per-token gradients within a response reduce variance and instability
Improved stability, efficiency, and performance vs GRPO
MoE training simplified by removing Routing Replay
Practical benefits for RL infrastructure and scaling
